All wandering cells are in the "Hematopoietic System" section
TermsIdentify this __ A, be specific.Sub-chapterSpecificity (for the same structure type)Description
Mesenchymal CellCellFixed CellUsually not seen in slides, use for stem cell
FibroblastCellFixed CellFX: secrete, produce and arrange ECM (collagen), wound healing
Very thin and dark nucleus
Mast CellCellFixed CellFX: inflammatory and allergic reaction, immediate hypersensitivity reaction
Numerous basophilic granules in cytoplasm (can obscure nucleus),
developed from basophil, metachromatically stained
Adipocyte (Fat Cell)CellFixed Cell
Unilocular (White) AdipocyteCellAdipocyte (Fat Cell)FX: thermal insulator, shock absorber, pigment deposition
"signet-ring," nucleus is on one side, for lipid storage,
Multilocular (Brown) AdipocyteCellAdipocyte (Fat Cell)FX: heat production (non-shivering thermogenesis)
Mostly found in infants
Plasma CellCellFX: produce antibody
Basophilic cytoplasm, eccentric nucleus, heterochromatin form cartwheel,
derived from B lymphocytes
Macrophage (Histiocyte in CNT)CellFixed CellFX: immune surveillance, phagocytosis
Connective tissue, spleen, lymph node, thymus, bone marrow
Derivatives:
- Dust Cell, in lung
- Kupffer Cell, in liver
- Langerhans Cell, in epidermis
- Microglia, in nervous tissue
- Osteoclast, in bone
Kupffer Cell (Perisinusoidal Macrophage)CellMacrophageLiver
Dust Cell (Alveolar Macrophage)CellMacrophageLung
Collagen FibersStructureExtracellular FiberFX: provide tensile strength
Most abundant, 4 types:
Type I - F resistance - skin, tendon, ligament, bone, capsule, fibrocartilage
Type II - P resistance - cartilage (hyaline & elastic)
Type III - increases kx - blood vessels, lymphoid
Type IV - filtration - basal lamina
Elastic FibersStructureExtracellular FiberFX: provide elasticity, respond to stretch & distension
Wave-like fibers, contain Elastin (protein) and Microfibrils (glycoprotein),
in blood vessels and elastic cartilage
Reticular FibersStructureExtracellular FiberFX: provide supporting framework, scaffold
Web-like fibers, contain type III collagen, in hematopoeitic, lymphoid
and glandular organs (kidney, liver, spleen, lymph node, bone matrix)
Amorphous Extracellular Substance
(Ground Substance)		Structure
